basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 34.' and it opens '(Vers. 34.) Et concepit adhuc, et peperit filium, et dixit: Nunc mecum erit vir meus,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 34.) Et concepit adhuc, et peperit filium, et dixit: Nunc mecum erit vir meus, quia peperi ei tres filios: ideo vocavit nomen ejus Levi. Ubi nos legimus, Apud me erit vir meus, Aquila interpretatus est, applicabitur mihi vir meus, quod Hebraice dicitur (ילוה), ILLAVE, et a doctoribus Hebraeorum aliter transfertur, ut dicant, prosequetur me vir meus, id est, non ambigo de amore in me viri mei: erit mihi in hac vita comes, et ejus dilectio me ad mortem usque deducet, et prosequetur: tres enim filios ei genui.
